_help.about: The player's movement table (PlanetPlayer reads it at start; restart the game after editing). Speeds in m/s, rates in m/s², times in seconds, distances in metres. The feel is Melee's spacies: heavy, snappy, committed jumps.
_help.speed: Top speeds on the ground: walk, sprint (double-tap forward and hold), sneak (hold Shift), aim (while a tool is charged, on the ground only; design §N says charging NEVER slows you, so aim_mps equals sprint_mps and is kept only for code that reads it), swim. swim_accel: how quickly you get up to swimming speed. double_tap_s: the most time between the two taps of forward that start a sprint.
_help.ground: accel: how fast you reach speed. friction: how fast you stop (lower = longer slide). turnaround_keep: pushing the other way at speed keeps this much of your old speed for a brief skid, then you go. turnaround_min_mps: below this there's no skid.
_help.overspeed: Faster than your run speed on the ground (out of a roll, a wall-jump chain, a swing) while pushing the same way, you slow by only decay_mps2, so momentum carries.
_help.traction: Multiplies ground accel and friction by what's underfoot: lower = slidier (a longer slide on stop). wet is shallow water and rain-soaked ground.
_help.air: Asymmetric gravity (design §J): gravity_up_mps2 is the pull while you rise (1.9, tuned by Claude Code so a held sprint bound lands about 50 m out: it peaks about 19 m up; a held standing jump about 15 m; a tap about 1.9 m) (low, an Earth-strength body on a 1/10 planet, so a bound carries far), gravity_down_mps2 while you fall (Earth or stronger, so nothing floats: the arc is a shark fin). gravity_mps2 is kept only as the old single value for code that hasn't split yet; the down value is the one to match it. jump_mps: take-off speed. jump_release_cut: letting go of jump while still rising cuts your rise speed to this share (tap = a hop, hold = the full bound). sprint_jump: take-off speed multiplied by this at a sprint. fast_fall_mps: press crouch after the apex to drop at once at this speed. max_fall_mps: terminal speed (a real body's, about 50). NO AIR STEERING (design §R): air_accel and air_steer_mps are 0; your velocity is fixed from take-off to the next contact. The body still turns freely with the look direction (body_turns_free).
_help.landing: squat_s: the frames of landing squat (no jump, no steering). heavy_squat_s: after a fall higher than heavy_fall_m (about a body length). dip_m: how far the view dips in the squat. min_drop_m: running off a bump lower than this (without jumping) is no landing at all.
_help.redirect: Every contact re-aims your momentum to where you are looking (design §R): landing, bounce, wall jump, cling or swing release. keep_by_angle: how much speed survives, by the angle (degrees) between your incoming velocity and the new direction, as [angle, share] points, interpolated: a small correction is nearly free, a right angle keeps about half, a full turnaround almost nothing. A perfect tech multiplies the kept share by perfect_gain (and may exceed 1 for small angles); a missed tech by miss_scale. No tech beats the geometry. ceiling_mps: where a perfect chain tops out in practice (120 km/h; the risk, not a wall); sanity_mps: the hard physics limit just above it, used wherever a max is needed.
_help.bounce: The branch bounce (design §J): land on TOP of a branch, ledge or trunk top (a surface you can stand on, not a face) after a fall of at least min_fall_m and press right click within window_frames, and the landing is a perfect one that turns your downward speed into forward speed toward where you look: carry of the fall speed, times gain. Missed: an ordinary landing with the usual roll rules. A bounce is a chain link (it counts toward wall_jump.chain_cap and it alternates feet). up_scale: the bound off it, as a share of air.jump_mps (added by Claude Code with the build).
_help.bounds: Alternating feet (design §J): every landing, bounce and kick alternates the planted foot, left, right, left. The torso leans foot_lean_deg toward the planted side and the cloak hem swings hem_swing_deg with it, so the body lilts in rhythm even with the legs hidden. The camera never bobs with it.
_help.slide: [NOT WIRED YET — design §Z.] The sprint slide: press the tech button (right click) while sprinting on the ground (faster than min_mps) and you drop into a slide with carry of your speed, slowing by friction_mps2 (scaled by traction: long on wet, sand, snow); slope_gain adds speed downhill and takes it uphill; you steer only steer_deg_per_s; it ends under end_mps or when you let go of right click, standing back into the run with the speed you have left. Jumping out of it is a low long hop that keeps the speed (a chain link). A slide into a wall or trunk without a tech is an impact. Every slide start plays the cloak flurry (audio.json).
_help.roll: The ninja landing roll: press the tech button (right click; Shift also works, design §Z) within window_frames of touching down after a fall higher than landing.heavy_fall_m. A roll takes no fall damage up to safe_m; past that, damage_scale of the normal fall damage (it still fires above max_m but only softens). It turns the fall into forward speed: your run speed plus carry of the fall speed (max_mps only a sanity limit). It rolls len_per_m metres per metre fallen (at least min_len_m, at most len_cap_m); no steering or jumping during it. Missed: the normal squat and full fall damage.
_help.fall_damage: A drop higher than safe_m (metres, from the top of the fall) hurts: per_m hit points for each metre over. Measured by height, so a fast-fall out of a hop never hurts.
_help.impact: Hitting a wall, trunk or rock at more than safe_mps (straight into it) without a tech (a wall jump or cling within the window) hurts: per_mps health for each m/s over. Fast enough, it kills.
_help.wall_jump: Right click is the tech button; what you touch decides the move. On a wall, cliff, trunk or ruin face in the air: press within window_frames (physics frames at 60 a second) of touching it. Let go within tap_frames and it's a wall jump; hold and you cling. A wall jump kicks you off back the way you came, angled angle_deg up, at speed_mps or your own approach speed if faster. Each chained wall jump (no ground, no cling between) multiplies that by chain_gain, up to chain_cap jumps; max_mps is only a physics sanity limit. min_wall_steepness: how steep a face must be. noise_m: how far creatures hear the kick. kick_frames: the kick animation (the first two frames are the crouch). A cling holds for cling_hold_s, slipping down at cling_slide_mps, then you slide off. Letting go of right click (or jumping) out of a cling still springs you off, at cling_jump_scale of a kick's speed, and starts the chain over (only a perfect tap chains); crouch drops you off instead. speed_mps is the kick even from a standstill: at the heavy gravity, 11 m/s at 58 degrees is about 1.5 m up and 5.8 m/s out.
_help.swing: Catch and swing (right click in the air, held, near a branch, bamboo or vine too thin to kick off): a handhold within catch_reach_m of your hands, ahead and not below you, toward where you look, on wood between min_radius_m and max_branch_radius_m thick (thicker is a wall-jump surface); you must be moving at least min_air_mps. You swing as a pendulum (gravity_scale of the pull: under 1 so the swing keeps its own slower rhythm now that the jump's gravity is heavy) with the speed you came in with, and can hang as long as you like (hang_damping slowly settles you). Let go (release right click, or jump) and you fly on with release_carry of the swing's speed. What you hold decides the rest (data/handholds.json): come in faster than its break speed and it snaps (you fly on with snap_speed_keep of your speed); it bends under you by its flex (flex_gain of your speed, springing at flex_hz, flex_damping), and on letting go the spring gives back its snapback as a push, a launch if you let go on the rebound. Hanging heavier than it bears (you weigh 1 plus load_per_item per carried thing), it gives way after give_way_s. A swing is a chain link.
_help.vines: Hanging vines on wet, warm-country trees (trees whose drawn vine amount is at least min_vines): up to max_per_tree hang from limbs higher than min_anchor_m, len_m long (a range), a handhold every step_m. radius_m: how thick (a vine is swung on, not climbed).
_help.run_pose: The ninja run: the body leans forward lean_walk_deg at a walk to lean_sprint_deg at a sprint, lean_accel_deg more while speeding up, leans back lean_stop_deg while stopping, and turn_lean_deg into turns; the head stays level. Between walk and sprint speed the arms trail back (arm_trail_deg from hanging; 90 would be level), flared out arm_spread_deg from the sides, elbows a touch bent (elbow_bend_deg), bobbing arm_bob_deg with each stride; they keep trailing through jumps, lag arm_lag_s behind when you slow, and blend back in over blend_in_s. Any action takes them at once.
_help.body: player_scale: the player's height against the rig (1 = 1.57 m to the top of the hood; 0.92 is about 1.44 m). The collision capsule, the eyes and the camera scale with it. Folk and other cloaked figures keep their own heights (data/creatures).
_help.climb: [CHANGING — design §V: climbing becomes hold right-click (cling) + move; E stops starting climbs. Not built yet.] On a tree's branches (the handholds): graph_trunk_mps is the body's speed during a reach up or round a trunk, graph_limb_mps along a limb; trunk_beat_s / limb_beat_s the pause after each reach; min_reach_s the shortest a reach can take (a short one still takes this long). simple_mps: climbing a trunk that has no handholds. reach_m: how far ahead a trunk can be for E to start climbing. grab_s: how long a hand takes to reach for something (a stuck spear) while climbing.
_help.burden: Carrying more than free_items things (the inventory's carry slots), each thing more makes you slow_per_item slower (never below min_speed of your normal speed), climb climb_slow_per_item slower, noise_per_item louder, and lean lean_per_item radians further forward. Felt, never shown as a number.
_help.wet_ground: soaked_rain_mm_h: rain this heavy (mm per hour) soaks the ground fully (traction falls to 'wet'); lighter rain soaks it partly. dry_s: after the rain stops, how long soaked ground takes to dry.
_help.unstick: Stuck is touching something and going nowhere: wedged between two walls (a trunk and a shrub's stem), held off the ground (under a root, in a fork), or caught on a crease of the ground. After stall_s moving slower than stall_mps, you're nudged nudge_m out along the free direction nearest to where you push. ground_jam_s: caught on the ground alone, you're freed after only this long (a hitch you barely feel).
_help.super_meter: The super meter (design §S): PERFECT techs (wall jump, bounce, roll, hop landing, swing release inside their windows) fill it, and so does LANDING A HIT on an opponent (fill_per_hit, and fill_per_critical for a critical); a missed or late tech only stops the run, it doesn't drain. fill_per_perfect: how much one perfect adds (0-1); chain_bonus_per_link: extra per link of the current chain, so long clean chains fill fastest. Spending: with any meter, hold a tool's charge past its normal full window and it overcharges (data/combat.json overcharge), which empties the meter on release. It never decays; only spending or dying (reset_on_death) clears it. NPC shinobi keep the same meter.
_help.camera: mouse and stick sensitivity. first_person_body: in first person, see your own hands, cloak edges and boots when you look down (false: nothing of your body shows; it still casts its shadow).
